nodes.label: Public history
nodes.date_label: Earlier public practices · US training discussions 1975 · The Public Historian 1978 · coverage through 2000
nodes.description: Historical research and interpretation undertaken with public institutions, communities and audiences. Professional service, collaborative authorship, preservation and popular uses of the past pose different questions about who sets the agenda and controls its presentation.
nodes.representative_figures_and_works: Robert Kelley: “Public History” (1978); G. Wesley Johnson: UCSB public-history training discussions (1975), documented by Kelley (1978); Michael Frisch: A Shared Authority (1990); Dolores Hayden: The Power of Place (1995); Roy Rosenzweig: The Presence of the Past (1998); David Thelen: The Presence of the Past (1998); Luli Callinicos: “The People’s Past” (1986); Raphael Samuel: “Local History and Oral History” (1976).

representative_people.context: Articulates a US programme of historical work in government, business and public institutions.
Co-develops the UCSB training initiative described by Kelley; this is a programme role, not sole authorship of public history.
representative_people.works: UCSB public-history training discussions (1975), documented by Kelley (1978)

representative_people.context: Examines editing and mediation between oral interviews and public presentation.
Connects urban landscapes with collaborative public interpretation.
Co-studies everyday engagement with the past in the United States.
Co-studies participation and historical authority beyond professional institutions.
Discusses South African popular history, worker education and community struggle.
Offers a British local/oral-history interlocutor; not a derivative of US professional training.

nodes.scope_note: The US professional programme is one formation. British local/oral practice and South African worker education enter as distinct interlocutors. Neither all public memory nor every popular historical product is equated with professional public history. Museum practice, Indigenous authority and non-Anglophone formations need fuller treatment.

strands.focus: Editing, documentary forms and audiences mediate historical testimony.

strands.focus: Callinicos connects popular historical writing to unions, resistance, language and audiences in South Africa.

nodes.label: Medical & health history
nodes.date_label: Earlier medical scholarship · social-medicine interventions 1930s · later social histories · coverage through 2000
nodes.description: Studies medicine, illness, healing and health in their historical settings. Practitioner scholarship, institutional histories, patient perspectives, public health and colonial or gendered experience coexist and contest what should count as medical knowledge and whose records matter.
nodes.representative_figures_and_works: Henry E. Sigerist: Socialized Medicine in the Soviet Union (1937); Roy Porter: “Lay Medical Knowledge” (1985); Dorothy Porter: Health, Civilization and the State (1999); Barbara Duden: The Woman Beneath the Skin (English edition 1991); Megan Vaughan: Curing Their Ills (1991); Steven Feierman: The Social Basis of Health and Healing in Africa (1992); John M. Janzen: The Social Basis of Health and Healing in Africa (1992).

representative_people.context: Combines medical historical scholarship with contested social-medicine and insurance advocacy before the postwar social-history expansion.
representative_people.works: Socialized Medicine in the Soviet Union (1937)

representative_people.context: Investigates lay knowledge and action within eighteenth-century medical encounters.
Studies public health through institutions, social conflict and citizenship.
Historicizes women’s embodied experience through a physician’s records.
representative_people.works: The Woman Beneath the Skin (English edition 1991)

representative_people.context: Examines colonial medical discourse and power in African settings.
Co-edits historical and social inquiries into health and therapeutic practices in Africa.
representative_people.works: The Social Basis of Health and Healing in Africa (1992)

representative_people.context: Co-edits interdisciplinary studies of African healing institutions and practices.
representative_people.works: The Social Basis of Health and Healing in Africa (1992)

nodes.scope_note: An enduring field with several programmes, not a school founded by the Society for the Social History of Medicine or its 1988 journal. Sigerist prevents a simple doctors-to-social-historians replacement story. Africa is represented by distinct projects, not a regional proxy. Asian, Latin American and Indigenous medical historiographies, clinical scholarship and histories of psychiatry require fuller treatment.

strands.title: Medical scholarship and social medicine
strands.focus: Sigerist links medical history with political arguments about health provision; his Soviet appraisal remains contested.

strands.title: Public health, welfare and the state
strands.focus: Health administration and citizenship are investigated through political and social institutions.

strands.title: Gender and embodied experience
strands.focus: Duden studies bodily experience through historically situated medical records.

nodes.label: Urban history
nodes.date_label: Earlier city histories · postwar expansion · Urban History Yearbook 1974 · coverage through 2000
nodes.description: Studies cities and urbanization through institutions, populations, built environments and connections beyond city boundaries. Local reconstruction, quantitative mobility research, colonial spatial analysis and histories of segregation or public landscapes form different approaches.
nodes.representative_figures_and_works: H. J. Dyos: Urban History Yearbook programme (1974); Sam Bass Warner Jr.: Streetcar Suburbs (1962; second edition 1978); Stephan Thernstrom: Poverty and Progress (1964); Thomas J. Sugrue: The Origins of the Urban Crisis (1996); Anthony D. King: Colonial Urban Development (1976); William Cronon: Nature’s Metropolis (1991); Dolores Hayden: The Power of Place (1995); Lynn Hollen Lees: “The challenge of political change” (1994).

representative_people.context: Organizes a British and international urban-history community, as Reeder’s 1979 appreciation records.
Studies the making of Boston suburbs through transport and building.
Uses linked local records to investigate mobility while raising representativeness as a problem.
Connects racial exclusion, institutions and industrial restructuring in Detroit.
representative_people.works: The Origins of the Urban Crisis (1996)

representative_people.context: Examines colonial spatial arrangements and social power, particularly Delhi.
Relates urban markets and processing to rural resources and production.
Connects urban landscapes and public historical interpretation.
Questions restricted urban biographies and the relative neglect of politics.

nodes.scope_note: British institution-building and US quantitative urban studies do not define one school or exhaust the field. Cities are not self-contained units. Delhi adds a specific colonial inquiry; wider Asian, African, Latin American and medieval/early-modern historiographies remain underrepresented. Journal milestones mark consolidation, not the first historical study of cities.

strands.title: Field organization and methodological debate
strands.focus: Dyos’s community-building and Lees’s later criticism show an open, contested research field.

strands.title: Transport, building and suburbs
strands.focus: Warner’s Boston case links infrastructure and the development of residential space.

strands.title: Urban mobility and linked records
strands.focus: Thernstrom tests mobility through census, tax and other local records.

strands.title: Race and industrial change
strands.focus: Sugrue studies exclusion and deindustrialization through Detroit institutions.
strands.works: The Origins of the Urban Crisis (1996)

strands.title: Colonial power and urban space
strands.focus: King’s Delhi study examines spatial arrangements as expressions of social and political power.

strands.title: Cities and hinterlands
strands.focus: Cronon follows commodities between rural production and urban processing and exchange.

strands.title: Public landscapes and interpretation
strands.focus: Hayden connects place-based interpretation with urban social histories.
